question.problem:
Find the limit at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}+1 & \text{ for }\,x<0 \\ 1 & \text{ for }\,x=0 \\ {e}^{-x}+1 & \text{ for }\,x>0.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{x}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}({e}^{x}+1) \\  & ={e}^{0}+1 \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{-x}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}({e}^{-x}+1) \\  & ={e}^{-0}+1 \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $2,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}f(x)=2.
$$
